newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares to see continuation of bull trend.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares to see continuation of bull trend.

text.p: Belgian shares ended easier on Tuesday, the last day of the forward market accounting period, but still look well established in their overall bull trend despite possible consolidation in the near term, analysts said.
The Bel-20 leading share index .BFX, which has soared to record highs from beneath 1,900 at the start of the year, fell 7.64 points or 0.37 percent from the previous close to 2,080.94.
"With a strong dollar, low rates and large amounts of cash to be spent, we should see gains in the weeks ahead," said Stefan Casteleyn, analyst at broker Corluy and Co.
He said financials were still his favourite sector.
This was because of the low interest rate environment.

Casteleyn considered chemical stock Solvay, down 2.28 percent at 21,450 francs after disappointing many in the market last Thursday with its preliminary 1996 profits, was now approaching attractive levels again.
The share soared after breaking the 19,500-franc level in early January, peaking at 23,300 on January 23 - the top of what turned out to be a negative, head and shoulders chart pattern.
Elsewhere, retailers Delhaize and Colruyt bucked Tuesday's down trend, climbing 0.76 percent to 1,990 francs and 0.49 percent to 15,325 respectively.
Dollar-sensitive Delhaize benefited from continued strength in the U.S. currency, dealers said.
But Colruyt, considered a quality stock, was now beginning to look rather expensive, one analyst noted.

Car distributor D'Ieteren was a prominent loser on the Brussels cash market, dropping 5.6 percent to 6,230 francs, after car rental firm Avis Europe - in which it has a 77.1 percent stake - said it would float on the London stock market.
Generale Bank analysts said they recommended investors to reduce their position in D'Ieteren as its upward potential may be coming to an end.
